$comment: The ~10 free-tier hardening items (SPEC 12): the plan spine for tenants with no paid Entra. Order is the intended sequence. goalId links to the catalogue goal's step where one exists.

items.name: Enable security defaults
items.description: Security Defaults provides a set of identity protections when the organization is not using a custom Conditional Access design.

items.name: Create and test emergency access accounts
items.description: Dedicated emergency accounts provide another administrative route when normal access fails. Test the route before an incident makes it necessary.

items.name: Review legacy authentication use
items.description: An inventory of older sign-in paths helps identify applications that need attention before authentication rules change.

items.name: Retire app passwords
items.description: App passwords keep older applications dependent on a credential that does not complete an interactive MFA check. Replace that dependency before retiring the credential.

items.name: Review per-user MFA settings
items.description: Consistent MFA management reduces conflicting settings and unexpected prompts. Keep enforcement in place throughout the transition.

items.name: Use separate accounts for admin work
items.description: Separating admin work from everyday activity reduces the exposure of privileged access.

items.name: Review Global Administrator access
items.description: Global Administrator has broad authority. Reviewing why each assignment exists can uncover access that no longer needs that level of privilege.

items.name: Review guest access
items.description: External access can outlast the project that needed it. Reviewing sponsors and current purpose helps identify guest access that should end.

items.name: Review inactive accounts
items.description: Reviewing inactive-account candidates can uncover access that is no longer needed. Missing activity still needs an owner check.

items.name: Move to stronger sign-in methods
items.description: Moving from phone codes to stronger approved methods can reduce reliance on telephone-based authentication. Test the replacement before removing a method people still use.
